newsitem.title: USA: Stokely says charge caused covenant violation.
newsitem.headline: Stokely says charge caused covenant violation.

text.p: Stokely USA Inc said Thursday that a nonrecurring charge related to its decision to restructure its canned vegetable business and write off some debt had caused the company to be in violation of certain financial and other covenants.
It said required consents had been received from holders of all affected issues to amend those covenants to put the company back in compliance.

Stokely today reported a net loss of $20.9 million, or $1.84 per share, for the fiscal year ended March 31, including a previously announced nonrecurring charge of $13.5 million, or $1.19 a share, for the restructuring and write-off.

Stokely said sales volume and pricing for canned vegetables were largely unchanged during the fourth quarter compared to a year earlier. But for the year, sales of canned vegetables decreased on lower volume, partially offset by higher prices.
The company said it expects to see cost reductions of $12 million on a full year basis from its restructuring, though less than half of that was realized in fiscal 1997 due to timing issues.

Stokely said selling prices in the processed vegetable markets are currently depressed, due primarily to excess industry inventories. Reduced planting in sweet corn for canning could result in improved prices and margins in the second half of fiscal 1998, it said.
"However, the significant margin pressure that currently exists is likely to prevail for most of the first half of fiscal 1998," Chief Executive Stephen Theobald said in a news release.
